small_guidance:
- Switch to NHWC layout for x and out (channels-last) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) becomes contiguous along IC; this enables vectorized loads on the inner ic loop instead of strided per-channel gathers.
- Add larger autotune configs (BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_SP=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2-4) and drop the 32/64 small tiles — the (OC=64, OH*OW=15876) shape benefits from wider N-tiles; also try BLOCK_OC=64 BLOCK_SP=256.
- Hoist `oc_offs * K` and `in_row_base` once outside the ic loop, and precompute the kh*IW + kw offset table as a constexpr 2D grid via tl.static_range to reduce inner-loop integer arithmetic.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, OutSpatial-tile), inner reduction over K = IC*KH*KW using `tl.dot` on [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SP] tiles. Current kernel does scalar FMA via broadcasting (`w[:,None] * x[None,:]`) which doesn't use tensor cores; switching to tl.dot on fp16/tf32 accumulate-fp32 will give a large boost on Ada.
- Use channels-last input layout (NHWC) and pack weight as [OC, KH*KW*IC] so the K-dimension is contiguous; load BLOCK_K=32 slabs per iteration and feed directly into tl.dot.
- Consider a persistent kernel where each program iterates over multiple (n, oc_tile, sp_tile) work items to amortize launch overhead, given the small per-tile work for KH=KW=3.
